title: Zooarchaeology by Mass Spectrometry (ZooMS) for Bone Material - Acid Soluble Protocol
author: Samantha Brown
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf5bjq2n

steps.title: Prepare 0.6 M Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)
steps.instruction: Prepare 1000 mL of 0.6 M HCl under a fume hood using glassware.

substeps.instruction: Carefully add 50 mL of 37% (v/v) HCl to 950 mL ultrapure water.
Mix gently.

steps.title: Prepare 50 mM Ammonium Bicarbonate (AmBiC) Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 1000 mL of 50 mM AmBiC buffer, pH 8, using a clean glass bottle.

substeps.instruction: Weigh out 3.95 g of AmBiC powder and transfer to the bottle.
Dissolve in 800 mL of ultrapure water and mix by gently inverting.
Fill up to 1000 mL with ultrapure water and mix by gently inverting.

steps.title: Prepare 5% (v/v) Trifluoroacetic Acid (TFA)
steps.instruction: Prepare the solution in a brown glass bottle under a fume hood using a glass syringe/pipette (no plastic).

substeps.instruction: Pipette 19 mL ultrapure water first.
Slowly add 1 mL TFA stock solution.
Mix carefully.

steps.title: Prepare Wash Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 1000 mL of 0.1% (v/v) TFA in ultrapure water.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of TFA to 1000 mL of ultrapure water.
Mix by gently inverting.

steps.title: Prepare Conditioning Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 1000 mL of 0.1% (v/v) TFA in 50% (v/v) Acetonitrile (ACN).

substeps.instruction: Mix 500 mL ACN with 500 mL ultrapure water.
Carefully add 1 mL of TFA.
Mix by gently inverting.

steps.title: Prepare Trypsin Solution
steps.instruction: Resuspend freeze-dried Trypsin (20 µg) to a final concentration of 0.4 µg/µl.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend 20 µg Trypsin in 50 µL of Trypsin resuspension buffer.
Transfer to a labelled 0.5 ml tube and store at -20 °C.

steps.title: Sample Weighing
steps.instruction: Weigh bone samples into labelled microcentrifuge tubes in a dedicated wet chemistry lab (surfaces wiped with ultrapure water and 70% ethanol).

substeps.instruction: Archaeological samples: Weigh 10 mg - 20 mg bone chips or ~10 mg bone powder.
Modern samples: Weigh 5 mg - 15 mg bone chips or ~7 mg bone powder.
Record the weight.

steps.title: Acid Demineralization
steps.instruction: Demineralize samples and prepare blanks (empty tubes with HCl only).

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL of cold (4 °C) 0.6 M HCl (or enough to cover sample) to the tube.
Store in fridge at 4 °C until demineralization is complete (bone is flexible/spongy, no bubbling). Duration: 4-10 h for powders, 1 day to 2 weeks for others.
Centrifuge at 20,000 rpm for 1 minute at room temperature.
Remove acid supernatant into a new tube labelled with sample number and suffix 'AC' without disturbing bone residues.

steps.title: Buffer Exchange
steps.instruction: Transfer the acid supernatant to an ultrafilter for buffer exchange.

substeps.instruction: Place a 30 kDa ultrafilter (or 3 kDa/10 kDa for poorly preserved collagen) into a labelled tube.
Add 250 µL of acid supernatant, ensuring the tip does not touch the membrane.
Centrifuge at 3700 rpm at room temperature for 5 to 30 minutes until acid is pushed through (do not let filter dry out).
Add 500 µL of 50 mM AmBic and centrifuge at 3700 rpm at room temperature for 5 to 30 minutes until AmBic has passed through.
Add 100 µL (or 50 µL for limited samples) of 50 mM AmBic to the filter and mix carefully by pipetting.

steps.title: Collagen Elution
steps.instruction: Collect the AmBic supernatant from the filter.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 50 µL of the AmBic supernatant to a tube labelled 'EXT'.
Transfer the remaining 50 µL supernatant to a tube labelled 'SE' (store at -20 °C).
Adjust volumes if 50 µL of AmBic was used in the previous step (only 'EXT' tube needed).

steps.title: Trypsin Digestion
steps.instruction: Digest the collagen extract with trypsin.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µL of 0.4 µg/µl trypsin solution to the 'EXT' tube.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C (approx. 12 to 18 hours).
Centrifuge at 20,000 rpm for 1 minute at room temperature.
Add 1 µL of 5% (v/v) TFA to stop the trypsin reaction.

steps.title: C18 ZipTip Purification
steps.instruction: Purify peptides from the 'EXT' sample using C18 ZipTips. Set pipette to 100 µL and do not change volume; avoid pulling air through the filter.

substeps.instruction: Prepare separate tubes for each sample: 250 µL conditioning solution ('C'), 450 µL wash solution ('W'), and 50 µL conditioning solution in a 'COL' tube for collection.
Condition the tip: Rinse twice with 100 µL conditioning solution and discard.
Rinse tip twice with 100 µL wash solution and discard.
Resuspend the 'EXT' sample back and forth over the tip at least 5 times.
Rinse tip twice with 100 µL wash solution and discard.
Elute sample into the 'COL' tube using 50 µL conditioning solution, passing through the tip at least 5 times (do not go past the first pipette stop).
